name: Complex_Square_Root
questiontext:
Find, in the form \(a + bi\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are real, a square root of \[{{CT:0}}\]
\(a + bi\) = [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

How to enter: the imaginary unit \(i\) is typed as the letter i (or %i), and multiplication with a star. For example 3-2*i.
generalfeedback:
Let \[\sqrt{{CT:0}} = a+ib\] Squaring gives us \[{{CT:0}} = a^2 + 2abi - b^2\] Therefore equating the real part\[{{CT:1}} = a^2-b^2\] and the imaginary part\[{{CT:2}} = 2ab\] Hence \[b=\frac{{CT:2}}{2a}=\frac{{CT:3}}{a}\] \[{{CT:1}}={{CT:4}}-\frac{{CT:5}}{{CT:4}}\] \[{{CT:6}}=0\] Finding the positive solution of this equation as a quadratic in {{CT:7}} gives \[{{CT:4}}=\frac{{{CT:1}}+\sqrt{{{CT:8}}+{{CT:9}}}}{2}=\frac{{{CT:1}}+\sqrt{{CT:10}}}{2}=\frac{{{CT:1}}+{{CT:11}}}{2}={{CT:12}}\] Therefore \[ a= {{CT:13}} \mbox{   and   } b = \frac{{CT:3}}{{CT:13}}={{CT:14}}\]

or \[ a= {{CT:15}} \mbox{   and   } b = \frac{{CT:16}}{{CT:13}}={{CT:17}}\]
